title: The Trans-Saharan Gold Trade (7th–14th Century) — The Metropolitan Museum of Art
excerpt: The Metropolitan Museum of Art explains that gold moved through trans-Saharan trade networks and notes that Mansa Musa's arrival in Cairo in 1324–25, carrying a very large quantity of gold, was associated with a sharp disruption in the gold market. Treat specific quantities and the scale or duration of the price effect cautiously because accounts differ.

title: Sahel: Art and Empires on the Shores of the Sahara — The Metropolitan Museum of Art
excerpt: The Metropolitan Museum of Art describes Mansa Musa's 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca via Cairo as forging connections across regions. It also links his return to contributions to Timbuktu's development as a center of Islamic study. Avoid implying that one ruler alone created Timbuktu's scholarly importance.

title: The Mali Empire — National Geographic Education
excerpt: National Geographic Education describes the Mali Empire as reaching a height of strength during Mansa Musa's reign, with prosperity connected to the empire's position in African trade networks. It identifies Timbuktu as an important center of knowledge and describes Musa's 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca.
